report_text:
I’ll document verified Sephora and Ulta tools for this value-focused shopper.

Basic loyalty and sale details are coming together — now I’ll dig into site search, filters, and policies.

I’ve mapped the core sorting and rewards features — next I’ll verify promotions, returns, and supporting shopper research.

Assortment and sale coverage look solid — now I’ll confirm the final loyalty and deal sources.

Core evidence is verified — now I’ll check a few remaining feature pages before drafting.

## 1. Sephora: site features and shopping tools

- **[Retailer-specific]** Tiered Savings Event discounts by loyalty tier: 30% off Sephora Collection and 20% off for Rouge, 15% off for VIB, 10% off for Insider with code ALLONSALE, listed as Beauty Insider members only in store and online ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Recurring Beauty Offers page requiring a promo code for each deal, for example free headband set with \$100 spend using UNREADY and Rouge-exclusive beauty bag with \$150 spend using INTHEBAG ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Time-bound markdown assortment described as up to 50% off select beauty on in-stock merchandise, stackable with the Savings Event code subject to terms ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Free Beauty Insider loyalty program with three annual-spend tiers — Insider free to join, VIB at \$350/yr, Rouge at \$1,000/yr — and Beauty Insider Cash redemption starting at 500 points for \$10 off, plus a Rouge-only 2,500 points for \$100 reward ([Beauty Insider | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-insider)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Subscription value lever: 5% off with Auto-Replenish subscription delivery, online only ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Insider free-shipping benefit and same-day-delivery offer with minimum spend, for example free same-day delivery with \$75 minimum using code SPEEDY ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).

## 2. Ulta Beauty: site features and shopping tools

- **[Retailer-specific]** Free Ulta Beauty Rewards program with Member 1 point per \$1, Platinum at \$500/yr 1.25 points per \$1, Diamond at \$1,200/yr 1.5 points per \$1, with points never expiring for Platinum/Diamond while status is maintained ([Ulta Beauty Rewards: Points for Dollars Off & Perks | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/rewards/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Points-to-dollars redemption ladder starting at 100 points = \$3.00, scaling to 2,000 points = \$125.00, redeemable in store and online on qualifying purchases ([Ulta Beauty Rewards: Points for Dollars Off & Perks | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/rewards/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Transaction coupons that include prestige and fragrance, for example \$10 off \$50, \$15 off \$75 or \$20 off \$100 with code GIFTS, valid Nov. 1-8, 2026 ([Ulta Coupons, Promo Code, Coupon Code | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/coupons/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Explicit coupon exclusions that shape net-price math: CHANEL, Dyson, Beauty Steals, 5 for \$5 / 5 for \$10, Black Friday deals, clearance, gift cards and marketplace orders are excluded ([Ulta Coupons, Promo Code, Coupon Code | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/coupons/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Mass-to-prestige continuum in one basket, described as allowing a \$7 drugstore mascara and a \$70 prestige serum in the same basket with loyalty points across all of it, plus salon services driving repeat trips ([Sephora vs Ulta: Who's Winning the Beauty Retail War?](https://www.42signals.com/blog/sephora-vs-ulta-beauty-retail-war/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Discovery surfaces for value comparison: homepage sections labeled Trending now and New Arrivals / New Beauty Products on ulta.com ([Ulta Beauty | Makeup, Skin Care, Fragrance, Hair Care & Beauty Products](https://www.ulta.com/)).

## 3. Retailer-specific evidence on how shoppers discover, evaluate and buy

- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora protects prestige positioning and price integrity and competes on exclusive curation and launch access, while Ulta spans accessible to prestige price points, so identical prestige items are often price-matched but Ulta provides more drugstore/masstige alternatives in the same cart ([Sephora vs Ulta: Who's Winning the Beauty Retail War?](https://www.42signals.com/blog/sephora-vs-ulta-beauty-retail-war/)).
- **[General beauty retail]** 88% of US beauty shoppers consider ratings and reviews when making a beauty purchase, 67% consider photos/videos from other shoppers, and 89% say they trust ratings/reviews for the buy decision, based on 26,340 US consumers surveyed May 2023 ([PowerReviews survey highlights strong pockets of consumer spending](https://www.cosmeticsdesign-europe.com/Article/2023/09/19/PowerReviews-survey-highlights-strong-pockets-of-consumer-spending)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Discovery is a relay: Google is first stop for 43%, with 57% starting on Instagram, YouTube, TikTok or AI; when a product is found on TikTok, 72% search for it on Google and only 7% buy directly through TikTok at that moment, based on 511 beauty consumers ([57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search](https://searchengineland.com/beauty-consumers-google-search-493828)).
- **[General beauty retail]** YouTube creators are rated very trustworthy by 14.1% versus 8.6% for TikTok creators; YouTube leads for tutorials while TikTok is nearly competitive with Google only for dupes/alternatives ([57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search](https://searchengineland.com/beauty-consumers-google-search-493828)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Value scrutiny is rising: 54% of executives see restricted spending as greatest risk, McKinsey notes cooling of the \$450 billion beauty market, and shoppers are described as easily price-comparing online with AI search accelerating comparisons ([How consumer demand for value is changing beauty shopping](https://www.glossy.co/beauty/how-consumer-demand-for-value-is-changing-beauty-shopping/)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Dupe-seeking is mainstream value behavior, not only lowest-price buying: 42% seek less expensive alternatives to high-end products and 64% of Gen Z and 67% of millennials use dupes to save money, with one in three beauty shoppers having purchased makeup dupes seen on social media ([Beauty Dupes & Aspirational Beauty: How to Capture Gen Z & Millennial Spending](https://www.cosmeticsandtoiletries.com/research/consumers-market/news/22923675/beauty-dupes-aspirational-beauty-how-to-capture-gen-z-millennial-spending)).

## 4. How this persona's traits show up at Sephora

- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Starts from need and value, not from the viral product: treats a \$38 viral blush as one candidate among 3-5 options, shortlists via creator side-by-sides then requires parity evidence on wear/finish across customer reviews before any substitution; price_sensitivity 0.90 drives the wide set, research_depth 0.85 drives the verification step.
- **[Inference – hypothetical, Scenario A]** Discovery: TikTok/YouTube awareness → general search for dupe/comparison → Sephora category and brand pages; seeks shade match, finish, wear-time and failure complaints; compares 3-5 brands and reads 6-25 reviews; buys \$14 alternative only if multiple recent reviews plus photos/video show comparable longevity, otherwise defers — evidence-supported that TikTok is strongest for dupes discovery while validation happens elsewhere ([57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search](https://searchengineland.com/beauty-consumers-google-search-493828)).
- **[Inference – hypothetical, Scenario B]** \$50 foundation with strong longevity proof versus \$22 with mixed wear reviews: calculates cost-per-expected-use from wear-time and repurchase risk; chooses higher-priced option only if multiple recent reviews consistently report longer wear/fewer repurchases, otherwise retains deferral or verifiable lower-priced option — quality_priority 0.75 tempers price_sensitivity 0.90 (evidence-supported that shoppers scrutinize whether products deliver and view serums vs cleansers as differentially splurge-worthy ([How consumer demand for value is changing beauty shopping](https://www.glossy.co/beauty/how-consumer-demand-for-value-is-changing-beauty-shopping/))).
- **[Retailer-specific – evidence-supported]** Times replenishment to verifiable promos: waits for Savings Event tier discount or Beauty Offers code and free-shipping threshold, and factors Beauty Insider Cash at 500 points = \$10 into net cost ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers)).
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Rejects premium without efficacy proof: if premium claims lack corroborating review themes on durability/performance, rejects despite prestige or packaging; prestige_priority 0.10 means brand alone never closes the gap.
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Research-effort rule: scales depth to ticket size, consumption frequency and return hassle — full 3-5 brand, 6-25 review comparison for high-use/hard-to-return items, abbreviated check for low-ticket easily returned trials; stops when last several reviews add no new attribute information and rank-order cannot plausibly change by more than expected saving net of time/return hassle.
- **[General beauty retail – evidence-supported]** Treats sponsored endorsements as low weight due to 24% distrust of influencer recommendations and demand for demonstrable results, requiring independent review volume/recency and user photos/video before switching ([Gen Z Beauty Trends 2025: Authenticity, Inclusivity | Attest](https://www.askattest.com/blog/research/gen-z-beauty-trends)).

## 5. How this persona's traits show up at Ulta Beauty

- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Exploits Ulta's continuum to compare across tiers in one place: pits prestige against mass/masstige equivalents and drugstore staples side-by-side, using filters for price/rating concepts and Trending/New as candidate sources only, never as proof.
- **[Retailer-specific – evidence-supported]** Calculates net price after verifiable coupon and points: tests whether \$10 off \$50 / \$15 off \$75 / \$20 off \$100 applies to the basket given prestige included but CHANEL/Dyson/clearance/Beauty Steals excluded, and adds points value from 100 points = \$3 up to 2,000 points = \$125 ([Ulta Coupons, Promo Code, Coupon Code | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/coupons/), [Ulta Beauty Rewards: Points for Dollars Off & Perks | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/rewards/)).
- **[Inference – hypothetical, Scenario C]** 30%-off product still above alternatives: treats percentage as non-trigger; keeps cheaper comparable as baseline and buys discounted item only if durability/cost-per-use evidence closes the gap, otherwise waits — hypothetical illustration of discount-skepticism, evidence-supported that value-driven shoppers trade down or trade up to value sizes rather than chase a badge ([How consumer demand for value is changing beauty shopping](https://www.glossy.co/beauty/how-consumer-demand-for-value-is-changing-beauty-shopping/)).
- **[Inference – hypothetical, Scenario D]** Larger size at higher ticket but lower cost-per-ounce: buys larger only if usage horizon justifies inventory without expiry/waste risk; otherwise chooses smaller with lower total outlay even at higher unit cost; observable action is checking size/price math manually when unit pricing is not displayed and deferring if horizon is uncertain.
- **[Inference – hypothetical, Scenario E]** Highly rated familiar product versus cheaper unfamiliar brand with promising performance: switches only with consistent recent review volume, photo/video evidence and clear return path; without that, retains familiar option despite price gap — brand_loyalty 0.30 enables switching but research_depth 0.85 gates it (evidence-supported that experimentation is replaced by considered switching with validation ([Gen Z Beauty Trends 2025: Authenticity, Inclusivity | Attest](https://www.askattest.com/blog/research/gen-z-beauty-trends))).
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Uses social comparisons for alternatives discovery: pulls dupe names from TikTok/YouTube/Reddit/beauty communities, then validates via general search and retailer review recency/volume; never purchases in-feed on popularity alone.

## 6. Sephora versus Ulta Beauty for this persona

- **[Retailer-specific]** Assortment fit differs: Sephora rewards prestige launch discovery and tiered-event savings on prestige, while Ulta lets value comparison span mass to prestige plus services in one loyalty account ([Sephora vs Ulta: Who's Winning the Beauty Retail War?](https://www.42signals.com/blog/sephora-vs-ulta-beauty-retail-war/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Loyalty economics differ: Sephora converts points to cash at 500 points = \$10 with higher tier unlocking larger event percentage, while Ulta converts points to cash on a rising scale to \$125 at 2,000 points and allows faster earn at Platinum/Diamond ([Beauty Insider | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-insider), [Ulta Beauty Rewards: Points for Dollars Off & Perks | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/rewards/)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Promotion mechanics differ: Sephora centers on code-gated Beauty Offers and twice-yearly Savings Event percentages, Ulta centers on threshold coupons including prestige plus Beauty Steals-type steals with many exclusions — both require checking terms before counting savings ([Sephora Coupons, Promo Codes & Coupon Codes | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com/beauty/beauty-offers), [Ulta Coupons, Promo Code, Coupon Code | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com/coupons/)).
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Versus Trend-Driven shopper: Trend-Driven starts from viral item and settles for a dupe; this persona starts from value and treats viral as one of several candidates — Scenario A at either retailer shows broader initial set, deeper review parity check, and willingness to buy neither if justification is insufficient.
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Versus Sensitive-Skin and Time-Constrained shoppers: same depth as Sensitive-Skin but checks price-per-use, durability and failure complaints rather than ingredients/irritation; opposite of Time-Constrained — spends time to save money rather than spending money to save time.
- **[Inference – hypothetical]** Stop-and-decide rule applied at both: cease cross-retailer comparison when additional searching cannot plausibly change rank-order by more than expected saving net of time and return hassle, then buy best-value verified option or defer; price sensitivity never means assuming lowest ticket is best value nor that similar claims equal similar results.

## 7. Evidence quality and gaps

- **[Retailer-specific]** Strong verification for loyalty and promo existence from retailer pages themselves, but exact review-filter labels, sort options, and unit-price display on sephora.com and ulta.com were not verified in sources reviewed and are not listed as existing features.
- **[General beauty retail]** Review influence is well-quantified for US beauty (88% consider, 89% trust), but data on filtering specifically for wear, finish or durability complaints is missing; the persona's 6-25 review depth is a modeling assumption, not an observed norm ([PowerReviews survey highlights strong pockets of consumer spending](https://www.cosmeticsdesign-europe.com/Article/2023/09/19/PowerReviews-survey-highlights-strong-pockets-of-consumer-spending)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Dupe prevalence (64-67% use) and price as primary driver (58% cite price) are documented, but willingness to pay more for proven longevity is inferred from value-scrutiny commentary rather than directly measured price-performance tradeoff rates ([Beauty Dupes & Aspirational Beauty: How to Capture Gen Z & Millennial Spending](https://www.cosmeticsandtoiletries.com/research/consumers-market/news/22923675/beauty-dupes-aspirational-beauty-how-to-capture-gen-z-millennial-spending), [Gen Z Beauty Trends 2025: Authenticity, Inclusivity | Attest](https://www.askattest.com/blog/research/gen-z-beauty-trends)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Return-path clarity matters to the switching rule, yet retailer return windows in third-party comparisons conflict (30-day full refund vs 60-day credit variations) and were not verified on retailer help pages in this pass, so no window is asserted here.
- **[Inference]** No evidence was found that every product has a direct dupe or that similar marketing claims predict similar performance; analysis assumes non-equivalence until independent performance proof is shown.
